summary: Raleigh County, WV state fire tower built 1928 (60 ft, not the 75 ft planned); removed in the 1980s; no source found describing the site today.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7'x7' cab
facts.status_note: Removed in the 1980s per the register, which gives no exact year; no source found describing the site today

events.note: Built 1928 by the five men the register names; 1928 newspaper notice announced a planned 75-foot tower, but the register and a 1962 article describe 60 feet
A crew of 16 men was set to begin a telephone line from the tower to Freezeland Mountain
Observer Ray Redden of Crow; visitors welcome under the observer's supervision during fire seasons
Registered July 19, 2016; nominated by Ronnie Scarbro

evidence.supports: built in 1928 by Pop Wriston, J.J. Goulden, John Hammond, Pat Kirk and Wint Lilly
evidence.quote: Built in 1928 by Pop Wriston, J.J. Goulden, John Hammond, Pat Kirk, and Wint Lilly, Round Knob Lookout provided views of the Beaver Creek, Little Beaver Creek, and Glade Creek watersheds.

evidence.supports: 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab; removed in the 1980s
evidence.quote: Round Knob was a 60-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7'x7' cab. It was removed in the 1980s.

evidence.supports: 1928 newspaper notice: planned 75-foot steel observation tower; state game and fish commission announced construction
evidence.quote: construction on the new 75-foot steel observation tower for forest-fire wardens to be located on Round Knob, Raleigh county, will start within two weeks.

evidence.supports: tower near the head of Little Beaver River; 3,000 feet altitude as stated in the 1928 notice
evidence.quote: Round Knob is located near the head of Little Beaver river and has an altitude of 3,000 feet above sea level.

evidence.supports: 1937 telephone line work from the Round Knob tower; crew of 16 men
evidence.quote: his crew of 16 men would begin work tomorrow on a telephone line in Richmond district, from the Round Knob lookout tower
A panoramic view of more than 20 miles of mountain range can be seen from the tower, which is 60 feet high.
Observer at Round Knob tower is Ray Redden of Crow.

evidence.supports: visitors welcome under the observer's supervision during fire seasons, March to May and October to December
evidence.quote: Visitors are welcome at the tower under the supervision of the observer during the fire seasons, March to May and October to December.

evidence.supports: agency listed as West Virginia Division of Forestry

corrections.why: 75 ft was the height announced for the planned tower in 1928; the register and a 1962 newspaper piece both describe the built tower as 60 feet.
The register says only 'It was removed in the 1980s.' No source read gives 1980. The removed event is left out of events[] until a year is found.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1928 notice gives a planned 75-foot tower; the register and the 1962 article give 60 feet for the built tower. The record uses 60 feet (18.3 m).
The register gives 2,730 ft (832 m); the 1928 notice and the 1962 article both say 3,000 feet. The register figure is kept in the record (832 m).

The 1928 notice credits the state game and fish commission with announcing construction; the Forest Lookouts page lists the West Virginia Division of Forestry as the agency. The record keeps the Division of Forestry.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 22.9 m reflects the planned 1928 height; the built height is 60 ft per two sources. Brief removal year 1980 is not in the register, which says only 1980s. The 1928 and 1962 newspaper passages were read as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, not from the original newspapers. No source found about the site today, including after a web search. The register and Forest Lookouts pages disagree on elevation and the agency at build time.
